title: Diagramming & Graphs — Where It Stands
thesis: One of the most complete planes in the library: 25 notations all rendered by one engine, over a native deterministic layout engine and a NetworkX-tier graph-algorithm suite; math and molecule diagrams are genuinely constraint-solved via autodiff. The old dot.exe dependency is demoted to an optional viewer — diagram layout is now engine-native. Guarded by ~1,790 assertions.

lanes.note: 25 notations (DN0-DN24), ~21 Haro faces, all as profiles over one renderer (stzDiagram), not separate tools; the domain list is closed by design
graph_layout.zig (GG1): barycentre crossing-reduction, seeded Fruchterman-Reingold force, bit-identical within and across processes
graph.zig (CSR): BFS/DFS, Dijkstra, A*, SCC, bridges, toposort, betweenness/closeness/PageRank/k-core/Louvain, MST, max-flow/min-cut; engine-implemented
Math (DN7) and molecule (DN11) layouts are solved by the engine's autodiff solver (StzEngineGrad*), with DragTo/Pin interactive re-solve
One renderer, three outputs: ToSVG (no device), ToPNG (GPU-backed), an ASCII visualizer; 24 node shapes; DOT export; no PDF/PostScript
Command-based edit session: Edit, Undo/Redo, EditLog, PickAt, RewireAnchor; illegal edits refused at the gesture; not a visual WYSIWYG editor
stzGraphRule and stzOrgRule feed the one CI gate (stzRuleReport): no-orphan-position, separation-of-duties; the rule catalogue is small
stzGraph exports DOT, JSON, GraphML and YAML (Dot(), RenditionAs); import parity thinner, GEXF/adjacency round-trips not all present
Notation-in-a-label (DN10), labels centred on cap-height not the em-box (DN12), curve clearance (DN13), solver-placed labels (SolveLabelsAfter)
Diagram layouts are engine-native; arbitrary large-graph visualization still leans on the optional dot.exe viewer: spline routing, nested clusters unmet
No standard graph generators (Erdos-Renyi, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz) and no isomorphism / graph-edit-distance surfaced
Diagrams emit interactive SVG and support programmatic re-layout (Relayout, DragTo); no built-in live pan/zoom/brush, the GUI plane's job

standouts: 25 notations as data profiles over one renderer
determinism as a guarantee: bit-identical layout across processes
constraint-solved layout via autodiff, which no mainstream tool does
gaps: meet the dot kill criterion (spline routing, nested clusters)
live interactivity via the GUI plane
dated: Read from the source on 2026-09-16, from a read-only main worktree
